judgments.reason: The passage states the policy prohibits use and actual possession of a personal electronic device during the school day, expressly including recess, lunch and time between classes.
The passage requires at least one method for parents and guardians to contact students during the school day, including policies for urgent emergency situations.
The passage lists mobile phones, tablets, laptops, smartwatches and bluetooth devices and excludes school issued or sanctioned devices used for educational purposes.
The passage states discipline for noncompliance shall not include expulsion or suspension and that enforcement shall ensure prevention of inequitable discipline.
The passage permits variations aligned with grade-level developmental needs while barring use and possession unless authorized under subsection (b).
The passage states nothing limits a district from setting restrictions on school grounds or during school-sanctioned activities beyond the school day.
The passage allows use in accordance with an IEP or a section 504 education plan.
The passage allows use where a healthcare provider provides in writing that it is necessary to treat a student's health condition.
The passage covers time spent off school grounds traveling to or from learning opportunities such as early college, dual enrollment or vocational sites.
The passage requires approval by the school committee, board or other governing body and solicitation of public input prior to approval.
The passage states the department's model policy goes into effect if no local policy is approved by September 1, until a local policy is approved.
The passage requires the department to provide guidance, recommendations and a model policy to assist schools and districts.
The passage requires annual notification to students and parents/guardians by September 1 and posting of the policy on the school website.
The passage requires each public school or district to adopt a policy on prohibiting student use of a personal electronic device.
The passage permits device use in accordance with an IEP or a section 504 plan.
The passage requires approval by the school committee or other governing body and public input beforehand.
The passage prohibits use and possession of a personal electronic device during the school day, including recess and lunch.
The passage requires at least one method for parents to contact students during the school day, including emergency situations.
The passage requires adoption of a policy before the start of the 2026-2027 school year.
The passage requires the department of elementary and secondary education to report to legislative committees on implementation of the policies.
The history entry records the House passing the bill to be engrossed on April 8, 2026 by 129 yeas to 25 nays, and the bill is a Senate document.
The history entry records appointment of a committee of conference in concurrence, indicating both chambers' members are reconciling the versions.
